text: Held W 12s more while pushing (14 m to summit); boulder slid off/rolled back: HUD now says 28 m to summit and 'The boulder: 38 m behind you'. No cue for why the push failed (drifted sideways?).

Session runs with clock=free (session info), not stepped as the brief says, so the world rots in real time while a screenshot-driven player orients. In ~3 minutes of trying to find the downhill/uphill side of the boulder on the 0.6 terrace, router, storage and cache all went DOWN and users fell 400->124. Weight bar hit max: 'too heavy to push uphill'.

Crosshair on 'search: DOWN (0%)... Hold E to patch'; held E for 5 s and then 8 s: no progress bar, no change at all. Either patching a module whose dependency is down is blocked (prompt should say so) or E does nothing here.

Same with storage (DOWN, the dependency): crosshair prompt 'storage: DOWN (0%), uses parser. Hold E to patch', held E 6 s: nothing. Also tried hold R 5 s and hold F 5 s on search: nothing. Drive log shows key_down/key_up (scancodes 8/9) accepted by the game. No feedback why the work does not start. W/Q/V/look all work.

Correction: holding E for 12 s on 'ui' (5%) DID patch it (now 'healthy (99%)'). Holds of 3-8 s earlier left no visible trace: progress seems to reset on release and no bar was visible in any after-release screenshot. At ~7 fps the time needed is far above the brief's 1-5 s; a player gets no sign that a short hold was 'almost there'.

Weight bar stuck at max ('too heavy to push uphill', 'Too heavy. It slides back.') even after retiring ui and search (12->10 modules) and patching ui, storage and cache to 97-99%. The screen never says what weight is made of or what brings it down, so I could not find a way out.

Open-issues list shows only the top 2 lines and '... and 5 more lines' while 8-10 issues are open: the other DOWN modules and their locations are invisible, and the order reshuffles, so I could not plan which module to reach next.

Users 0, health 0%, all listed modules DOWN, weight max: no message, no fail state, no hint what to do. The boulder just sits on the 0.6 terrace. Module labels on the boulder are shown only for a few modules, so 'core: facing you' could not be located by sweeping the crosshair.
